_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.english_concept: cursive / joined-up handwriting style (as a text style name)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'skrivstil' for the cursive/script generator style and any cursive practice-sheet copy. Keep 'kursiv' strictly for the italic style. If a page must serve both, name them separately and say so explicitly — that disambiguation is itself useful content a machine-translated competitor cannot produce.
phrases.good_example: Skriv ditt namn i skrivstil och kopiera det direkt till din bio.
phrases.avoid_when: Never use 'skrivstil' to label the italic/slanted style — that is 'kursiv'. Also avoid using 'kursiv' as the cursive label anywhere on the site.

phrases.english_concept: font / typeface (which of the two Swedish words to use)
phrases.usage_guidance: Default to 'typsnitt' in headings and marketing copy. Use 'teckensnitt' only when the sentence is genuinely about a Word/Windows font menu, where that is the string the user sees on screen. Do not stuff both into one title as near-synonyms.
phrases.good_example: Välj ett typsnitt och kopiera texten direkt.
phrases.avoid_when: Avoid 'teckensnitt' in casual/social headings; avoid 'typsnitt' when literally quoting a Windows/Office UI label.

phrases.english_concept: problem description: styled text renders as empty boxes / garbage characters
phrases.usage_guidance: Use verbatim as an FAQ heading on any sv page that explains why decorative Unicode may not render for everyone, and specifically why a styled Swedish name can lose å/ä/ö. Pair 'konstiga tecken' with 'fyrkanter' in the answer so both searched formulations are on the page.
phrases.good_example: Varför visas konstiga tecken istället för åäö när jag klistrar in namnet?
phrases.avoid_when: Not for titles/H1 — it is a symptom query, and the page's primary target should stay the tool/style term.

phrases.english_concept: collective term for å, ä, ö (the letters most at risk from decorative Unicode)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use in the FAQ answer that explains which characters a given Unicode style does and does not cover. The high-value honest statement for sv pages is that most decorative Unicode blocks have no å/ä/ö, so a styled Swedish name silently loses them — 'Mårten' becomes 'Marten', a different name. Say it in these words.
phrases.good_example: De flesta stilar saknar svenska bokstäver — å, ä och ö faller tillbaka till vanlig text.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'svenska bokstäver' as an H1 target — it is explanatory vocabulary, not a demand term. Do not call å/ä/ö 'diakritiska tecken' in user-facing copy (ä/ö are separate letters in Swedish, not accented a/o — saying otherwise reads as foreign).

phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the style label in the sv generator UI and in any style-list heading.
phrases.good_example: Små versaler — ᴘᴇʀғᴇᴋᴛ ғöʀ ᴇɴ ᴅɪsᴋʀᴇᴛ ʙɪᴏ.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'kapitäler' in the UI unless the page is specifically about typography as a craft.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'nicknamn'/'nick' in gaming-name sections; use 'användarnamn' only when talking about the account login field, and 'profilnamn' for the displayed name. Getting this three-way split right is a concrete quality signal against machine translation, which flattens all three to 'användarnamn'.
phrases.good_example: Byt ditt nicknamn till något snyggare — men kolla teckengränsen först.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'nicknamn' in copy about a real account/login field, or in any non-gaming context. Do not use 'smeknamn' for a gaming handle.

phrases.english_concept: copy and paste (as an everyday action)
phrases.usage_guidance: Write it in full in headings and instructions. For a button, 'Kopiera' alone is enough. Do not invent a Swedish clipping.
phrases.good_example: Kopiera texten och klistra in den i din bio.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not drop the particle ('klistra' alone is wrong). Do not use the English 'copy paste' in written page copy even though Swedes say it aloud — in text it reads as sloppy.

phrases.english_concept: the historical verb for inscribing runes -- evocative heritage framing, not a literal 'generate' verb
phrases.content_surface: flavor/intro copy for a rune-converter page (an evocative subhead), not a functional CTA
phrases.avoid_when: as a literal button/CTA label -- reserve for editorial framing only, since the tool doesn't physically carve anything and that risks overpromising authenticity

phrases.english_concept: invisible character(s) — the phrase for the blank/invisible-name trick
phrases.content_surface: page title / H2 for an invisible-character tool page
phrases.usage_guidance: Primary candidate term for an SV invisible-character feature/page, mirroring the role 'usynlig tegn' (NO-021) and 'görünmez karakter' (TR-002) play for their locales.
Use for casual-register symbol-decoration copy; keep SV-016 (specialtecken) for neutral/technical framing (FAQ, accessibility notes).

Neutral/technical default term — pairs with SV-005/SV-015 for casual-register copy elsewhere on the page. Mirrors DA-005 (specialtegn) and NO-006 (spesialtegn), the same word's cognates in the other two Nordic locales researched this pass.
phrases.avoid_when: hero/title copy where a warmer, casual phrase (snygga bokstäver, coola tecken) fits better
